subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS embedded Dashboard browser receive only configured shared token/password auth, or may it also receive native device/operator tokens?
rationale: The linked reports propose conflicting auth boundaries for the same browser injection path, and changing this behavior affects credential isolation and upgrade compatibility for existing macOS users.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Keep native device tokens limited to native websocket clients, update this PR to cover the new endpoint-change path, and close or redirect the parity sibling after proof.

options.title: Preserve native-token parity
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction so Dashboard browser injection can use resolved native/operator auth.

options.title: Require a narrower design note first
options.body: Pause both branches until a maintainer documents the Dashboard auth precedence and the upgrade behavior for users without shared tokens.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Keep native device tokens limited to native websocket clients, update this PR to cover the new endpoint-change path, and close or redirect the parity sibling after proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the native macOS Dashboard window and later Dashboard/Gateway token hardening work.
